column5: Hey, I'm just theorizing.\nWe have no idea what will actually happen.\nWe just know one thing — The Triumvirate wants it destroyed.
column6: 嘿，我只是在推测。\n我们根本不知道实际会发生什么。\n我们只知道一件事——三人执政团想毁掉它。

column5: And that means they don't want anyone else to have it.\nSo there must be {i}something{/i} we can use it for, right?\nWe think that this is part of your destiny, [firstname].
column6: 也就是说，他们不想让任何人得到它。\n所以它一定{i}有{/i}什么我们能派上用场的地方，对吧？\n我们认为这是你命运的一部分，[firstname]。

column5: And that means they don't want anyone else to have it.\nSo there must be {i}something{/i} we can use it for, right?\nWe think that this is part of your destiny, [firstname].
column6: 也就是说，他们不想让任何人得到它。\n所以它一定{i}有{/i}什么我们能派上用场的地方，对吧？\n我们认为这是你命运的一部分，[firstname]。

column5: My destiny...?
column6: 我的命运……？

column5: It's not a coincidence that all of this happened at once.\nWe find the idol just as you realize your potential...?\nPerhaps it's that potential we need to be using.
column6: 这一切同时发生绝非巧合。\n我们刚发现灵像，你就觉醒了潜能……？\n或许我们需要的正是那份潜能。

column5: Basically, it's going to happen like this.\nWe'll get to Mazeo, and Damek will start your training.\nWhen you feel comfortable enough, we'll bring you to the idol.
column6: 基本上，事情会这样发展。\n我们到达马泽奥后，达梅克会开始训练你。\n等你觉得足够自如了，我们就带你去灵像那里。

column5: You'll use your power to tap into it, and empower our army.\nThen you'll help Damek lead our final assault on Balteus.\nWe'll take down The Triumvirate in their own home.
column6: 你会用你的力量与之共鸣，强化我们的军队。\n然后你会协助达梅克领导我们对巴尔泰乌斯的最后一击。\n我们要在他们的老巢里扳倒三人执政团。

column5: Wow...
He really has it all planned out, huh?
column6: 他还真是计划得滴水不漏啊。

column5: Yeah. Smooth sailing once we get to Mazeo.\nBut I think it would be too dangerous to leave right now.\nIt's almost night time. We should rest and leave in the morning.
column6: 是啊。等我们到了马泽奥就一帆风顺了。\n但我觉得现在出发太危险了。\n天快黑了。我们该休息一下，明早再走。

column5: I agree. I made good time on my journey over here.\nWe'll still be on schedule, even if we stop to rest.\nSpirits know I need it after the long trek I just took.
column6: 我同意。我这一路过来走得挺快。\n就算停下来休息，我们也不会误了日程。\n刚走完这么长的路，我确实需要休息，众灵作证。

column5: Resting does sound pretty good right now.\nIt's been such a hectic day, I'm overwhelmed.
column6: 现在休息听起来确实不错。\n今天实在太忙乱了，我有点吃不消。

column5: Yeah, and it'll give us time to discuss {i}other{/i} matters.\nI'm down to rest, Ulric. Just point us in the right direction.
column6: 是啊，这也让我们有时间讨论{i}其他{/i}事情。\n我赞成休息，乌尔里克。指个方向就行。

column5: Not so fast. Let's hang out for a bit, first.\nIt's still early enough that we can have plenty of fun.\nGo look around. I won't be too far behind, alright?
column6: 别急。我们先待一会儿。\n时间还早，足够我们好好玩一场。\n去四处转转吧。我随后就到，好吗？

column5: Oh, sure!
column6: 哦，当然！

column5: Valessa and Fortaime leave the table, and start looking around.{w}\nThat's what I would've done, were it not for the earlier argument.{w}\nUlric and Pro look at me, and let out deep sighs.
column6: 瓦莱莎和福泰姆离开桌子，开始四处打量。{w}\n要不是先前那场争执，我也会这么做。{w}\n乌尔里克和普洛看着我，深深叹了口气。

column5: I'm gonna go grab a drink.\n[firstname], when you're ready, take any room you want.\nWe'll head to The Outlook at dawn, and journey down to Mazeo.
column6: 我去弄点喝的。\n[firstname]，你准备好了就随便挑个房间。\n我们黎明时分出发去瞭望台，然后南下前往马泽奥。

column5: I'm gonna go grab a drink.\n[firstname], when you're ready, take any room you want.\nWe'll head to The Outlook at dawn, and journey down to Mazeo.
column6: 我去弄点喝的。\n[firstname]，你准备好了就随便挑个房间。\n我们黎明时分出发去瞭望台，然后南下前往马泽奥。

column5: He gets up and walks away, leaving me alone with Pro.
column6: 他起身走开了，留下我和普洛单独待着。

column5: Look, I'm sure you're processing a lot all at once.\nBut you're not alone. We're about to go to war.\nI'm overwhelmed too, and so is Ulric.
column6: 听着，我知道你一下子要消化很多东西。\n但你并不孤单。我们即将开战。\n我也吃不消，乌尔里克也一样。

column5: He might not show it, but I'm sure he's scared.\nThere's never been a battle like this before.\nAll we can do is play with the hand we've been dealt.
column6: 他可能不表现出来，但我肯定他也害怕。\n以前从未有过这样的战斗。\n我们只能打好手里这副牌。

column5: Pro has now permanently joined the party.
column6: 普洛现已永久加入队伍。

column5: I'll see you around, alright?\nWatching everybody drink is making me thirsty.\nIf you miss me, you'll know where to find me.
column6: 回头见，好吗？\n看大家喝酒把我看渴了。\n要是想我了，你知道去哪儿找我。

column5: He leaves the table, and goes to grab a drink.\nAll I can do is hang out for a while, and then go to sleep.\nMaybe I could talk to Pro for some more information, too.
column6: 他离开桌子，去拿喝的。\n我能做的只有先待一会儿，然后去睡觉。\n或许我还能找普洛聊聊，多打听些消息。

column5: Whatever I did, though? \nThis would be my final night in Valinorth...
column6: 不过，无论我怎么做？\n这都会是我在瓦利诺斯的最后一夜……

column5: Click the arrow in the top right corner to advance the story.\nOtherwise, feel free to explore Peregrino at your leisure.
column6: 点击右上角的箭头推进剧情。\n否则，你可以随意探索佩雷格里诺。

column5: Oh, hey Zamira!\nIt's good to see you again.\nI was starting to worry you might...
column6: 哦，嘿，扎米拉！\n很高兴再见到你。\n我还在担心你可能会……

column5: Oh, come on now.\nThere's no need to worry about me.\nI'd worry about Valinorth. There's no more gate guard.
column6: 哦，别这样。\n没必要为我担心。\n你该担心瓦利诺斯。已经没有城门守卫了。

column5: Oh yeah, I guess that {i}was{/i} your job.\nI'm glad to see that you got everything done.\nDid you happen to... touch that sword, by any chance?
column6: 哦对，我猜那{i}确实{/i}是你的工作。\n很高兴看到你把事情都办好了。\n你有没有……碰过那把剑？

column5: Absolutely not.\nI kept it under wraps the entire time.\nWe put it in The Grand Tree for safekeeping.
column6: 绝对没有。\n我一直把它原样封存着。\n我们把它放在巨树里妥善保管。

column5: Good idea. I'm just really curious.\nDamek was able to use it, however briefly.\nAnd not only that, but he had a vision too.
column6: 好主意。我只是太好奇了。\n达梅克竟然能用它，哪怕只是一瞬间。\n不仅如此，他还看到了幻象。

column5: Yeah, I was wondering about that.\nDidn't you guys find a new spirit idol in Mazeo?
column6: 是啊，我也在想那事。\n你们不是在马泽奥发现了一尊新的灵像吗？

column5: Yeah, I think he wants to harness it for power.\nI didn't stop to ask, but it's all he talks about now.
column6: 是啊，我想他是想借助它获取力量。\n我没停下来多问，但现在他满嘴都是这个。

column5: Well, isn't it inside your new HQ?
column6: 呃，它不就在你们的新总部里吗？

column5: Yeah — now that you mention it.
column6: 是啊——你这么一说。

column5: Didn't Damek frequent those underground tunnels?\nMaybe he was exposed to some level of spiritual energy.\nAt least enough to let him have a vision, or something.
column6: 达梅克不是常去那些地下隧道吗？\n也许他接触过某种程度的灵能量。\n至少足以让他看到幻象之类的。

column5: I... don't think that's how it works.
column6: 我……不觉得那是靠这种方式运作的。

column5: It's a possibility, at least give me that much.\nThat blade challenges {i}all{/i} of our understandings.
column6: 这是一种可能，至少承认这一点吧。\n那把剑挑战了我们{i}所有{/i}的认知。

column5: Alright, your theory has merit.\nIt's really odd — but it makes sense.\nCan you even imagine if it was true...?
column6: 好吧，你的理论有几分道理。\n这真的很古怪——但说得通。\n你能想象如果那是真的吗……？

column5: Maybe that's why Damek wants to harness its power.\nGiving regular people visions? He'd have an army of Seers.\nThere's no way The Triumvirate could fight back against {i}that{/i}.
column6: 也许这就是达梅克想借用它力量的原因。\n让普通人也能看到幻象？那他就能拥有一支先知大军。\n三人执政团根本没法对抗{i}那种{/i}东西。

column5: Whoa...\nHey, how'd you learn about this stuff anyway?
column6: 哇……\n嘿，话说你是怎么知道这些的？

column5: I overheard a few things, that's all.\nNo one is leaking intel or anything.
column6: 我只是偶然听说了些事，仅此而已。\n没人泄露情报之类的。

column5: Good. We can't have any moles.\nThe Rebellion, as it is — currently hangs on threads.\nIt's only thanks to that anomalous blade that we stand a chance.
column6: 很好。我们不能有内鬼。\n反抗军如今——已是岌岌可危。\n全靠那把异常的剑我们才有一线希望。

column5: Hey, you were working with [firstname]?
column6: 嘿，你之前是和[firstname]一起干活的？

column5: Hey, you were working with [firstname]?
column6: 嘿，你之前是和[firstname]一起干活的？

column5: Yeah, something like that.\nIt lasted all a couple hours.
column6: 是啊，差不多吧。\n总共也就持续了几个小时。

column5: What do you think about him?
column6: 你觉得他怎么样？

column5: What do you think about her?
column6: 你觉得她怎么样？

column5: I honestly have no idea.\nIt's hard to believe that our fate rests upon {i}one{/i} person.\nI don't think I could put my faith in somebody that way.
column6: 说实话，我完全不知道。\n很难相信我们的命运竟然系在{i}一个{/i}人身上。\n我觉得我没法那样去信任别人。

column5: Why not?
column6: 为什么不？

column5: It's a big gamble, isn't it? Too risky.
column6: 这是场大赌博，不是吗？太冒险了。

column5: Yeah, but faith is all about risk.\nYou believe in spite of overwhelming odds.\nYou fight, even when {i}everything{/i} tells you to stop.
column6: 是啊，但信仰本来就是关于冒险的。\n哪怕希望渺茫，你也选择相信。\n哪怕{i}一切{/i}都让你停下，你也依然战斗。

column5: Hmm...
You don't have to agree, but it's true.\nWithout faith, The Rebellion wouldn't even be here.\nAlestia would remain under The Triumvirate's grasp forever.
column6: 你不必同意，但这是事实。\n没有信仰，反抗军根本不会存在。\n阿拉斯蒂亚将永远陷在三人执政团的掌控之下。

column5: You have a point, Ulric.\nIt's impressive that you've come this far.
column6: 你说得有道理，乌尔里克。\n你们能走到这一步，真令人钦佩。

column5: And we still have a long way to go.\nBut we won't get there if people don't {i}believe{/i}.\nHave a little faith in us, alright Zamira?
column6: 而我们还有很长的路要走。\n但如果人们不{i}相信{/i}，我们就走不到那里。\n对我们多一点信心，好吗，扎米拉？

column5: Well, I can't say no to that.\nJust don't let me down, alright?\nWhen we make it through this, I'm buying drinks.
column6: 嗯，这个我没法拒绝。\n只是别让我失望，好吗？\n等我们熬过这一切，酒我请。

column5: Oh, you mean you aren't buying right {i}now{/i}?\nAnd here I was — buttering you up for nothing.
column6: 哦，你是说{i}现在{/i}你不请？\n我还在这儿——白拍你马屁了。

column5: Can you believe Damek's nerve...?
column6: 你能信达梅克有这么大的胆子吗……？

column5: Don't worry, he knows what he's doing.\nHe wouldn't act outside of Alestia's best interests.\nWhatever he's planning, I trust him.
column6: 别担心，他知道自己在做什么。\n他绝不会做出违背阿拉斯蒂亚利益的事。\n不管他在谋划什么，我都信他。

column5: Even if it means losing my tavern...?
column6: 哪怕这意味着我要失去我的酒馆……？

column5: I can't change my outlook, sorry.
column6: 抱歉，我的看法没法改变。

column5: Alright...\nAt least you can relate to me a little.\nWithout Valinorth, your job is gone too.
column6: 好吧……\n至少你还能稍微理解我。\n没了瓦利诺斯，你的工作也没了。

column5: Yeah, looks like we'll both be unemployed.\nMaybe we could look for a new job together.\nWe're all going to Mazeo, right?
column6: 是啊，看来我们俩都要失业了。\n也许我们可以一起找份新工作。\n我们都要去马泽奥，对吧？

column5: It's the closest place to go.\nBut I think the pirates have the monopoly on that place.\nYou think the new Rebel HQ will have a tavern at all?
column6: 那是最近的地方了。\n但我觉得那地方被海盗垄断了。\n你觉得新的反抗军总部会有酒馆吗？

column5: Beats me. But I know Mazeo has one.\nWhen we get there, how about we scout it out?\nStart looking in your comfort zone, and {i}then{/i} branch out.
column6: 我也不知道。但我知道马泽奥有一家。\n等我们到了那儿，不如去踩踩点？\n先从你熟悉的领域找起，{i}然后{/i}再拓展。

column5: Yeah, that's a good idea.\nThanks Zamira, you're a good guy.\nI hope you can find a new job as well.
column6: 是啊，好主意。\n谢了扎米拉，你是个好人。\n希望你也能找到新工作。

column5: I might ask Damek if he has any openings.\nI don't need money. Just food, and a place to live.\nHe's offering that to {i}everyone{/i} from Valinorth.
column6: 我可能会问问达梅克有没有空缺。\n我不要钱。只要食物和住处就行。\n他对{i}所有{/i}来自瓦利诺斯的人都提供这些。

column5: I guess he really {i}is{/i} a nice guy...\nBut he's taking Peregrino away from me.\nIt's hard to side with someone like that, you know?
column6: 看来他{i}确实{/i}是个好人……\n但他要夺走我的佩雷格里诺。\n很难站在那种人那边，你懂吗？

column5: I understand.\nDon't worry, everything will work out.\nWe'll need more barkeeps when this is all over.
column6: 我明白。\n别担心，一切都会好起来的。\n等这一切结束后，我们会需要更多酒保。

column5: Really?
column6: 真的？

column5: Yeah, of course!\nImagine the celebrations when we win.\nThis isn't permanent. You'll be fine.
column6: 是啊，当然！\n想象一下我们胜利时的庆祝吧。\n这不是永久的。你会没事的。

column5: Zamira, can I talk to you for a second?
column6: 扎米拉，能跟你说句话吗？

column5: Of course. What's up, Airen?
column6: 当然。怎么了，艾琳？

column5: I want to thank [firstname] for what he's done.\nDefying Damek's orders, and letting me keep Peregrino?\nThey deserve something, but I don't know what to do.
column6: 我想感谢[firstname]所做的一切。\n违抗达梅克的命令，让我保住佩雷格里诺？\n他们值得一份回报，但我不知道该怎么做。

column5: I want to thank [firstname] for what she's done.\nDefying Damek's orders, and letting me keep Peregrino?\nThey deserve something, but I don't know what to do.
column6: 我想感谢[firstname]所做的一切。\n违抗达梅克的命令，让我保住佩雷格里诺？\n他们值得一份回报，但我不知道该怎么做。

column5: Hmm...
I was thinking of offering him a permanent room.\nYou know, to stay here whenever he wants.\nShould I offer unlimited drinks as well?
column6: 我想过给他一个永久房间。\n你知道，他想来住就来住。\n要不要再提供无限量的酒水？

column5: I was thinking of offering her a permanent room.\nYou know, to stay here whenever she wants.\nShould I offer unlimited drinks as well?
column6: 我想过给她一个永久房间。\n你知道，她想来住就来住。\n要不要再提供无限量的酒水？

column5: Hmm...
Zamira, are you paying attention?
column6: 扎米拉，你在听吗？

column5: Does this offer of free drinks extend to his comrades?
column6: 这个免费酒水的承诺也适用于他的同伴吗？

column5: Does this offer of free drinks extend to her comrades?
column6: 这个免费酒水的承诺也适用于她的同伴吗？

column5: I suppose it would.
column6: 我想应该会吧。

column5: Alright, I'm sold!\nHere, I'll take you to see him right away.\nI'm so thirsty — this is going to be amazing!
column6: 好，成交！\n来，我这就带你去找他。\n我太渴了——这简直太棒了！

column5: Alright, I'm sold!\nHere, I'll take you to see her right away.\nI'm so thirsty — this is going to be amazing!
column6: 好，成交！\n来，我这就带你去找她。\n我太渴了——这简直太棒了！

column5: Zamira — whoa, let go!\nI want a gift for {i}them{/i}, not {i}you{/i}!
column6: 扎米拉——哇，松手！\n我要送礼给{i}他们{/i}，不是{i}你{/i}！

column5: Don't worry, he'll love it!\nEverybody — Airen is giving us free drinks!\nCome over here, let's celebrate for Peregrino!
column6: 别担心，他会喜欢的！\n各位——艾琳请大家免费喝酒！\n都过来，为佩雷格里诺庆祝！

column5: Don't worry, she'll love it!\nEverybody — Airen is giving us free drinks!\nCome over here, let's celebrate for Peregrino!
column6: 别担心，她会喜欢的！\n各位——艾琳请大家免费喝酒！\n都过来，为佩雷格里诺庆祝！

column5: Oh no.\nIs he serious right now...?\nThere's no way I have enough for everybody.
column6: 哦不。\n他是认真的吗……？\n我根本不可能有足够的酒请所有人。

column5: Yeah, you heard right! Free!
column6: 对，你没听错！免费！

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: I joined shortly after the occupation. The previous leader recruited me.\nIt seems that children with revenge on their minds was in both high demand {i}and{/i} supply.\nI grew up with Damek, and a bunch of other kids our age. They trained us all in war.
column6: 我是在占领开始后不久加入的。上一任领袖招募了我。\n看来怀着复仇之心的孩子，既需求旺盛，{i}又{/i}供应充足。\n我和达梅克，还有一群同龄的孩子一起长大。他们把我们全都训练成了战士。

column5: Ulric joined a little bit later. He's older, and was already trained.\nAs you could've guessed, I lost my family during the occupation. A common tale as of late.\nBut we're finally ready to take on The Triumvirate. We'll take back the future they stole.
column6: 乌尔里克稍晚一些加入。他年纪更大，而且早就受过训练。\n你可能已经猜到了，我在占领期间失去了家人。近来这种事很常见。\n但我们终于准备好迎战三人执政团了。我们要夺回被他们偷走的未来。

column5: He's a really nice guy, and we've shared a lot of the same struggles.\nThere's no one else I'd rather march into battle with. I mean it.\nHis tactics, his strategy — it's really something else.
column6: 他是个很好的人，我们经历过许多相同的磨难。\n要说并肩作战，我最想跟的就是他。我是认真的。\n他的战术，他的谋略——真的非同凡响。

column5: Watching him on the war table is nothing short of an honor.\nI can't wait to get an interview with the guy. His story needs to be told.\nAfter this all blows over, I'm sure he'll go down in history as a hero.
column6: 看他在作战沙盘前运筹帷幄，简直是一种荣幸。\n我迫不及待想采访他。他的故事值得被讲述。\n等这一切平息之后，我敢肯定他会作为英雄载入史册。

column5: Did you... not hear what I just said?\nI mean, of course he is. He's the best.\nNot only capable, but exceeding expectation.
column6: 你……没听见我刚说的话吗？\n我是说，他当然厉害。他是最棒的。\n不仅能力出众，还超出预期。

column5: Yeah, and the transition between leaders was pretty seamless.\nHe was close to our previous leader, so he picked up on a lot of stuff.\nIt's almost like he was being trained from the start to take over.
column6: 是啊，而且两位领袖之间的交接相当顺畅。\n他和我们上一任领袖关系很近，所以学到了很多东西。\n简直就像他从一开始就被培养着要接班。

column5: He's been obsessed with these underground tunnels, lately.\nHe wants our headquarters to be hidden, and well guarded.\nI think he's trying to strike a deal with the Mayor of Mazeo.
column6: 他最近迷上了那些地下隧道。\n他想让我们的总部既隐蔽又守备森严。\n我觉得他是想和马泽奥的市长谈笔交易。

column5: That means the Mayor is defecting from The Triumvirate. That's good.\nWe have a huge advantage as long as that secret isn't leaked.\nBut there's something else he's been talking about as well.
column6: 也就是说市长要叛离三人执政团了。这是好事。\n只要这个秘密不泄露，我们就握有巨大的优势。\n但他还谈起过另一件事。

column5: In the same tunnels he wants to claim, he discovered a spirit idol.\nA massive one, flowing with unfathomable amounts of energy.\nI think he wants to tap into it with that blade, and use that power.
column6: 在他想占据的那批隧道里，他发现了一尊灵像。\n一尊巨大的灵像，涌动着难以估量的能量。\n我觉得他想用那把剑与之共鸣，借取那份力量。

column5: You're living proof that idols can empower people, right?\nIf we could do that to our army? We'd be almost unstoppable.
column6: 你就是灵像能赋予人力量的活证据，对吧？\n如果我们能对我们的军队这么做呢？那我们几乎就无可阻挡了。

column5: With the right strategy, and that special blade? Of course.\nI'm just glad that Damek is the best strategist I've ever seen.\nThen there's you. I'm not so sure about you, yet.
column6: 有正确的战略，再加上那把特殊的剑？当然。\n我只是庆幸达梅克是我见过最出色的战略家。\n然后就是你。对你我还没那么有把握。

column5: With the right training, I think you'll be fine.\nSo that's what we'll do when we get to Mazeo. Train.\nAnd no complaining about the hours. The fate of Alestia is at stake.
column6: 只要训练得当，我想你会没事的。\n所以到了马泽奥我们就这么办。训练。\n还有，别抱怨训练时间长。阿拉斯蒂亚的命运危在旦夕。

column5: Oh, sure. What did you want to talk about?
column6: 哦，当然。你想聊什么？

column5: Join the club. Almost everybody lost a family member during the occupation.\nAt least it helps you relate to the others. You're not alone in this.\nI can't imagine tackling this struggle all by ourselves.
column6: 彼此彼此。占领期间几乎每个人都失去了亲人。\n至少这能让你和其他人产生共鸣。在这件事上你并不孤单。\n我无法想象只靠我们自己来面对这份苦难。

column5: Yeah, I guess you could say that. It's not an ideal place to be, though.\nIf the occupation never happened, and my family were here — that'd be better.\nBut you gotta make the best of what you have, so I can't really complain.
column6: 是啊，算是吧。不过这可算不上什么好处境。\n如果占领从未发生，我的家人还在——那会好得多。\n但你得善用自己所拥有的，所以我也没什么好抱怨的。

column5: Probably somewhere a lot safer than Mazeo, working on my next big hit.\nI'd be a totally different person, too. The last ten years were spent on training.\nIt's almost impossible to find time to myself, you know?
column6: 大概会在比马泽奥安全得多的地方，写着我的下一部大作。\n我也会是完全不同的人。过去十年都花在训练上了。\n几乎抽不出一点时间给自己，你懂吗？

column5: But most importantly, my family would still be here.\nI always wondered what kind of people they'd turn out to be.\nSo without the occupation, I'd probably stick by their side.
column6: 但最重要的是，我的家人还会在这里。\n我总在想他们会成为什么样的人。\n所以如果没有那场占领，我大概会一直守在他们身边。

column5: Not really. At least not in the way you'd think.\nIt was all about reconnaisance for me. Staying on the high ground.\nI mapped out a lot of Balteus, so our leader could come up with a plan.
column6: 算不上。至少不是你想的那样。\n我主要负责侦察。守在高处。\n我绘制了巴尔泰乌斯的大片地形，好让我们的领袖制定计划。

column5: When they raided The Triumvirate's castle, I stayed far behind.\nThey made sure that nobody got in my way, and I mapped the castle too.\nWe're going to take advantage of that map when we attack them again.
column6: 他们突袭三人执政团的城堡时，我远远地留在后方。\n他们确保没人妨碍我，我也把城堡的地图画了下来。\n等我们再次进攻时，会好好利用那张地图。

column5: I saw the corpse of our leader as Damek carried it out. It was horrible.\nAfter that, he buried it underneath Mazeo, in those tunnels he likes.\nBut with that blade, and the castle plans? One final attack is all we need.
column6: 达梅克把领袖的遗体抬出来时，我看见了。那场面太可怕了。\n之后，他把它葬在马泽奥地下，就在他喜欢的那些隧道里。\n但有了那把剑和城堡的图纸？我们只需最后一击。

column5: Well, I've known him for years, and he's never let me down.\nI don't think I've ever seen someone so strong. He's unbeatable.\nIf he went back to Alarinthia, he could {i}easily{/i} become its ruler.
column6: 嗯，我认识他多年，他从未让我失望过。\n我没见过比他更强的人。他无人能敌。\n要是他回到阿拉林西亚，他{i}轻轻松松{/i}就能成为那里的统治者。

column5: But he never gives up the chance to tell us how much he hates it.\nSo I guess we're stuck with him here on the mainland for a while.\nI wonder what he'll do once all of this blows over.
column6: 但他从不放过任何机会告诉我们他有多厌恶那里。\n所以我想，我们还得让他在大陆上多待一阵子。\n我很好奇等这一切平息后他会做什么。

column5: Of course you can! I can't think of anyone better.\nWith him by your side, you'll never be in real danger.\nDon't tell him I said that though. His ego needs to stay in check.
column6: 当然可以！我想不出比他更好的人选了。\n有他在你身边，你永远不会真正陷入危险。\n不过别告诉他是我说的。他那自尊心得有人压着点。

column5: Wait, are you serious!? Ulric has a perfect reputation.\nHe's never been bested in combat, and I don't think he ever will.\nI'll have to chalk that one up to being a simple inaccuracy in your vision.
column6: 等等，你是认真的！？乌尔里克的名声无懈可击。\n他在战斗中从未落败，我觉得以后也不会。\n那个我只能归结为你幻象里的一个小小误差。

column5: You're probably just being paranoid. He's a good man.\nThough I can see why you'd suspect something like that.\nHe's pretty reserved. He doesn't like talking about his past.
column6: 你大概只是多心了。他是个好人。\n不过我也能理解你为什么会那样怀疑。\n他相当内敛。不喜欢谈起自己的过去。

column5: But trust me, he's a valuable ally to both you and The Rebellion.\nI wouldn't push him away, you'll need him more often than not.\nWho knows — he may even open up to all of us one day.
column6: 但相信我，他对你和对反抗军都是宝贵的力量。\n我不会把他推开，你多半会常常需要他。\n谁知道呢——也许有一天他甚至会向我们所有人敞开心扉。

column5: Absolutely not. The man sure knows how to use that blade.\nI sure hope I'm never on the receiving end of his rage.\nHe'll be a key figure in every upcoming battle. I know it.
column6: 绝对不会。那家伙用起剑来确实了得。\n我只希望自己永远不会成为他怒火的目标。\n每一场即将到来的战斗他都会是关键人物。我敢肯定。

column5: If you want to know for sure, he's always up for sparring.\nI think the new rebel HQ will have tons of practice swords.\nMake sure to tell me if it gets that far, though. I'd love to watch!
column6: 你要是想弄个清楚，他随时都愿意切磋。\n我想新的反抗军总部会有大量练习用剑。\n不过要是真发展到那一步，记得告诉我。我很想看看！

column5: Well, I'm a bit of a gambler. I love to take risks, and have them pay off.\nAside from that, I like to write. I fancy myself an author, I guess.\nAfter this war, maybe I'll get to focus on that a little bit more.
column6: 嗯，我算是个赌徒。我喜欢冒险，喜欢看它们有所回报。\n除此之外，我喜欢写作。我自认算个作家吧。\n这场战争之后，也许我能多花点心思在那上面。

column5: Non-fiction, mostly. I like to chronicle the stories of important people.\nSo — and this is just an example — but yourself, and Damek.\nYou'll go down in history. But you need to be {i}real{/i}, not a legend.
column6: 主要是纪实。我喜欢记录重要人物的故事。\n所以——这只是个例子——比如你自己，还有达梅克。\n你们会载入史册。但你们得是{i}真实{/i}的人，而不是传说。

column5: Like I said, I hope to write more stuff when this war is over.\nI don't exactly have much time to myself, even on the best of days.\nIt's hard for the other rebels to find time, too. I need to eavesdrop.
column6: 就像我说的，等这场战争结束，我希望能多写点东西。\n就算状态最好的日子，我也没什么属于自己的时间。\n其他反抗军成员也很难抽出时间。我得靠偷听。

column5: Hey now, I'm not hinting at anything like that!\nI'd rather wait until things die down, to be honest.\nNo offense, but you haven't done anything noteworthy yet.
column6: 嘿，我可没在暗示那种事！\n说实话，我更想等事情平息下来再说。\n无意冒犯，但你还什么都没做过值得一书的事。

column5: Hopefully that will change with time, and {i}then{/i} we can talk.\nBut for now, I need to focus on Damek and the other rebels.\nYour story has yet to unfold — and as such, has yet to be written.
column6: 但愿随着时间会有所改变，{i}到那时{/i}我们再谈。\n但现在，我得把重心放在达梅克和其他反抗军成员身上。\n你的故事尚未展开——因此也尚未被书写。

column5: Not everything, I'd be a fool to try that. Just the important stuff.\nIf that's what I aim for, I'm sure I can get it all. Maybe...\nI just want to make sure that people's stories are told.
column6: 不是全部，那样做我就是个傻瓜。只是重要的部分。\n如果我只盯着那些，我肯定能全都记下来。也许吧……\n我只是想确保人们的故事被讲述出来。

column5: Important figures usually become exaggerated legends.\nI only want to ground them in reality, you know?\nThat way, history remembers who they {i}really{/i} were.
column6: 重要人物通常会变成被夸大的传说。\n我只想让他们扎根于现实，你懂吗？\n这样，历史记住的才是他们{i}真正{/i}的样子。

column5: Of course not. I mean, they never see me, so they {i}can't{/i} be mad.\nBut I'm not being creepy or anything. Just \"listening in\" here and there.\nIt'll be a lot easier to do in our new HQ, though. Wait 'till you see it!
column6: 当然不会。我是说，他们从来看不见我，所以也{i}没法{/i}生气。\n但我不是在做什么变态的事。只是偶尔“旁听”一下。\n不过在我们新总部里做起来会容易得多。等你见到就知道了！

column5: Nothing I can tell you! An author never spills his secrets.\nIf someone else can tell my stories, then what's the point?\nI take these to the grave — or at least, until I publish them.
column6: 没什么能告诉你的！作家从不泄露自己的秘密。\n如果别人也能讲我的故事，那还有什么意义？\n我会把它们带进坟墓——至少在出版之前是这样。

column5: I like to cook. Actually, I like it a lot. I'm always in the kitchen.\nI have to take it easy, though. I used to eat way too much. I was fat.\nBut that's almost a lifetime ago. It only took some practice in self control.
column6: 我喜欢做饭。其实，我非常喜欢。我总待在厨房里。\n不过我得克制一点。我以前吃得太多，很胖。\n但那几乎是上辈子的事了。只需练练自控力就行了。

column5: Well, self control, {i}and{/i} exercise. I'm always on the move.\nAside from that, I like to go to the theater. Plays are great nowadays.\nThat's pretty much it. I'm not the most exciting person, to be honest.
column6: 嗯，自控力，{i}还有{/i}锻炼。我总是闲不下来。\n除此之外，我喜欢去剧院。如今的戏剧很棒。\n差不多就这些。说实话，我不是最有意思的人。

column5: Wait — is that a compliment or an insult...?\nYou know what? Don't answer that, actually.\nI'll take it as a compliment. Thank you.
column6: 等等——这是夸我还是损我……？\n你知道吗？还是别回答了。\n我就当是夸奖吧。谢谢。

column5: Absolutely! It's so far to find a workout partner these days.\nWell, unless your idea of a workout is using practice swords.\nI prefer using daggers, and my fists. I focus on agility.
column6: 当然！如今想找个一起锻炼的人太难了。\n呃，除非你所谓的锻炼就是挥练习剑。\n我更喜欢用匕首和拳头。我注重敏捷。

column5: The enemy can't hurt you if you kill them first, right?\nAt least, that's what I like to tell myself. I seem useful in combat.\nI've never had any complaints, and Damek usually asks for my help.
column6: 只要先杀掉敌人，他们就伤不到你，对吧？\n至少我总这么告诉自己。我在战斗里还算有用。\n我从没被抱怨过，达梅克也常找我帮忙。

column5: There's one I really love. It's called \"A Tragedy in Balteus\".\nThe hero works for both the good guys {i}and{/i} the bad guys.\nThe good guys find out, and they kill him in cold blood.
column6: 有一部我特别喜欢的。叫《巴尔泰乌斯的悲剧》。\n主角同时为好人{i}和{/i}坏人效力。\n好人发现了，就冷血地杀了他。

column5: It turns out he was good all along, he was just using the bad guys.\nTheir hasty choice causes them to lose, and the bad guys kill them all.\nIt's really tragic, and ironic. Everything a good story needs!
column6: 原来他一直都是好人，只是在利用坏人。\n他们草率的决定导致落败，坏人把好人全杀了。\n真是既悲壮又讽刺。一个好故事需要的一切都有了！

column5: Yeah, there really is. There's a huge theater, but it's tucked away.\nMost people never see it, since it's right in the middle of the marketplace.\nBut there's a loyal following, and there's always something new to watch.
column6: 是啊，确实有。有一家大剧院，但藏得很深。\n大多数人从没见过，因为它就在集市的正中央。\n不过有一批忠实观众，而且总有新东西可看。

column5: I'd love to be a playwright, but I don't think that's my calling.\nI think I'm better off letting the masters tell their stories.
column6: 我很想当剧作家，但我觉得那不是我的天职。\n我想我还是让大师们去讲他们的故事更好。

column5: I'm not sure, actually. Maybe I'll focus on my writing career.\nBut I'd need to retire somewhere nice, and free of distraction.\nMazeo is just so {i}busy{/i}, it's hard to focus on anything.
column6: 其实我不确定。也许我会专注于写作事业。\n但我得退隐到一个又好又没干扰的地方。\n马泽奥实在太{i}热闹{/i}了，很难专注做任何事。

column5: Maybe I'll find someone special, and bring them along.\nThis is all up in the air, of course. A lot could change.\nI probably shouldn't plan it out. I'll play it by ear.
column6: 也许我会遇到一个特别的人，带上一起走。\n当然，这些都还没定。很多事都可能变。\n我大概不该计划得太细。走一步看一步吧。

column5: I'd say Valinorth — but I don't think that's going to happen.\nMaybe Balteus, if I can get used to the cold. It seems quiet there.\nWhen The Triumvirate is taken down, we can settle there for once.
column6: 我会说瓦利诺斯——但我觉得那不太可能。\n也许巴尔泰乌斯吧，如果我能习惯寒冷。那里似乎很安静。\n等三人执政团被扳倒，我们说不定能在那里安顿下来。

column5: Oh my, are you asking for yourself?\nEither way, the answer is no. I haven't had time for that.\nLove and war don't mix together, unless the formula is a tragedy.
column6: 哎呀，你是在替自己问吗？\n不管怎样，答案都是不。我没时间做那种事。\n爱情和战争混在一起，除非配方是悲剧。

column5: Whatever you feel like doing! We'll be free, and capable of anything.\nFar be it from me to tell you how to live your life. Do your thing.
column6: 你想做什么就做什么！我们会自由，无所不能。\n我可没资格教你怎么过日子。随你心意去做吧。

column5: I've been here for a couple weeks, much to Damek's dismay.\nHe wanted me to bring the blade to Valinorth, and get you {i}immediately{/i}.\nI guess maybe he thought the attack was going to happen right away.
column6: 我在这儿待了几个星期，这让达梅克很懊恼。\n他想让我把剑带到瓦利诺斯，{i}立刻{/i}把你带回来。\n我猜他可能以为进攻马上就要开始了。

column5: An outsider marching into Valinorth with a weapon would be a bad idea.\nThat's why I wrapped it up and gave it to Zamira to keep safe.\nI knew Mylus would give it to you, and you'd come here eventually.
column6: 一个外乡人拿着武器闯进瓦利诺斯可不是好主意。\n所以我把剑包好，交给扎米拉保管。\n我知道迈勒斯会把它交给你，而你最终会来这里。

column5: I knew we had spare time, so I decided to play it safe.\nBesides, Peregrino is a pretty cool place.\nAiren sure is fun to hang out with.
column6: 我知道我们还有余裕，所以决定稳妥行事。\n再说，佩雷格里诺是个挺不错的地方。\n和艾琳待在一起确实很有意思。

column5: Probably not. I mean it all worked out for the best.\nI got to relax here too, which is really hard to do these days.\nOverall, I wouldn't be concerned. It's such a minor change.
column6: 大概不会吧。我是说，结果一切都再好不过了。\n我也能在这儿放松放松，这年头可太难得了。\n总的来说，我不担心。不过是点小变动。

column5: He's capable of adapting, which is why he sent Ulric here as well.\nThe fact that Ulric is calm speaks volumes. Damek isn't mad.\nIf he was, I'd be in the middle of a huge verbal lashing right now.
column6: 他善于随机应变，所以才把乌尔里克也派了过来。\n乌尔里克这么平静就说明了很多。达梅克没生气。\n要是他生气了，我现在早就被骂得狗血淋头了。

column5: The Rebellion needed a neutral location between Mazeo and Valinorth.\nIt's pretty much the same distance away from both nations, after all.\nThey held meetings here, and conducted business free of geographical bias.
column6: 反抗军需要在马泽奥和瓦利诺斯之间有一个中立地点。\n毕竟这里到两国的距离差不多一样远。\n他们在这里开会，不受地理偏向地进行事务往来。

column5: It was especially important during the early days of The Rebellion.\nThe alliance between Valinorth and Mazeo was rocky at best.\nYou guys weren't exactly open to forming treaties with outsiders.
column6: 在反抗军早期，这一点尤为重要。\n瓦利诺斯和马泽奥之间的联盟充其量也只是摇摇欲坠。\n你们这些人当时并不怎么愿意和外人缔结条约。

column5: I think it's a pretty good idea, if you want to resettle Valinorth.\nAny future attackers will have to march right past Peregrino.\nCan't think of a better use than to station a capable army here.
column6: 如果你想重建瓦利诺斯，我觉得这是个相当不错的主意。\n将来任何来犯者都必须经过佩雷格里诺。\n我想不出比在这里驻扎一支精锐军队更好的用途了。

column5: Not much, to be honest. But probably more than most.\nI pride myself on picking up weird information.\nAnd if you're talking weird - they really fit the bill.
column6: 说实话，知道得不多。但大概比大多数人多一些。\n我引以为傲的就是能搜集到些稀奇古怪的情报。\n要说古怪——他们还真名副其实。

column5: Their rule goes really far back. Like, we don't know about a time {i}without{/i} them.\nA lot of people on Alestia consider them Gods, and say they created our world.\nBut there's no way to know for sure. They never answer questions like that.
column6: 他们的统治可以追溯到很久以前。久到我们不知道还有{i}没有{/i}他们的时代。\n阿拉斯蒂亚的很多人把他们当作神明，说他们创造了我们的世界。\n但无从确证。他们从不回答这类问题。

column5: It's really rare that they come out of their chambers. I've never seen it happen.\nAnd I'm starting to wonder if I ever will. I bet that's where we'll take them down.\nWe've tried to lure them out, but it never works. They see right through our tricks.
column6: 他们极少走出自己的居所。我从没见过。\n我开始怀疑自己到底见不见得到。我敢打赌我们会在那里将他们扳倒。\n我们试过引他们出来，但从没成功。他们一眼就能看穿我们的把戏。

column5: I wish I could tell you.\nNobody knows, and they'll probably never tell us.\nThey'll probably take that secret to their ever-nearing graves.
column6: 但愿我能告诉你。\n没人知道，他们大概也永远不会告诉我们。\n他们多半会把这个秘密带进越来越近的坟墓里。

column5: How old is our world again? Yeah, they're {i}that{/i} old.\nThey've been here since the dawn of time.\nI wonder how we'll kill people so strong...
column6: 我们的世界有多少年了？是啊，他们就有{i}那么{/i}老。\n自时间之初他们就在这儿了。\n我在想，我们要怎么杀死这么强的人……

column5: We have no idea. We just know about their cloaks.\nThey're given an affectionate nickname — white-cloaks.\nThey wear these beautiful white robes, trimmed with gold.
column6: 我们完全不知道。我们只知道他们的斗篷。\n人们给他们起了个亲昵的绰号——白袍。\n他们穿着华丽的白色长袍，镶着金边。

column5: Kind of like that blade you've got on your back.\nLeads more credence to the theory that they created it.\nKind of ironic, isn't it? Being killed by their own creation?
column6: 有点像你背上的那把剑。\n这让“是他们创造了它”的说法更有说服力。\n有点讽刺，不是吗？被自己的造物杀死？

column5: I'm not really sure that Gods exist.\nAt least, not in the conventional sense.\nIt's almost like that {i}blade{/i} is a God.
column6: 我不太确定神是否真的存在。\n至少不是传统意义上的那种。\n那把{i}剑{/i}倒几乎像个神明。

column5: It has the ability to repurpose our spiritual energy.\nThat's how they make their army, right?\nMaybe they used it to gain immortality, too.
column6: 它有能力重新利用我们的灵能量。\n他们就是这样组建军队的，对吧？\n也许他们也用它来获得永生。

column5: If that's true — then where did the blade come from?\nI'm terrified just thinking about it. What {i}is{/i} that thing?
column6: 如果那是真的——那这把剑又是从哪来的？\n光是想想我就毛骨悚然。那东西{i}究竟{/i}是什么？

column5: I don't think any ruler is truly evil.\nThe needs of a world and its people are always changing.\nI think they're out of touch on what Alestia needs right now.
column6: 我认为没有哪个统治者是真正邪恶的。\n一个世界及其人民的需求总是在变。\n我觉得他们已经不了解阿拉斯蒂亚现在需要什么了。

column5: And in their heads — I'm sure they consider themselves good.\nI'm sure they have a reason for all the terrible things they've done.\nI know The Rebellion sure does. Our hands aren't exactly clean.
column6: 而在他们自己看来——我相信他们自认为是善的。\n我相信他们为自己做过的所有可怕之事都有理由。\n我知道反抗军肯定也有。我们的手可不算干净。

column5: Either they made it, or they found it. Both options are terrifying.\nIf they found it, that means it came from somewhere. Another world, even.\nIn that case, how many worlds, how many people, were victim to its power?
column6: 要么是他们造的，要么是他们找到的。两种可能都令人恐惧。\n如果是找到的，那就意味着它来自某个地方。甚至是另一个世界。\n那样的话，有多少世界、多少人曾是它力量的牺牲品？

column5: On the other hand, if they created it? They must be almost unstoppable.\nIf they made it on their own, then by logic — they have to be stronger than it.\nDoesn't exactly fill you with confidence to march against them, does it?
column6: 另一方面，如果是他们造的？那他们必定几乎无可阻挡。\n如果他们是靠自己造出它的，按逻辑说——他们一定比它更强。\n这可不怎么让人有底气去讨伐他们，对吧？

column5: It seems like it, but there's no way to know for sure.\nWe've never been under anyone else's lead, right?\nI imagine it'll be chaotic at first, until we figure things out.
column6: 看起来是这样，但没法确定。\n我们从没在别人的领导下待过，对吧？\n我想一开始会很混乱，直到我们摸索出门道。

column5: It's not a turn-key operation. We're talking about ruling a world.\nDamek, or whoever ends up taking charge, will have to learn a {i}lot{/i}.\nAfter that, we just have to hope that the people accept new rulers.
column6: 这可不是一蹴而就的事。我们说的是统治一个世界。\n达梅克，或者任何最终掌权的人，都得学{i}很多{/i}东西。\n在那之后，我们只能祈望人民能接受新的统治者。

column5: A huge greatsword rests against the table.{w}\nIt's completely unattended, like someone left it here.{w}\nDid they do that on purpose, or did they lose it?
column6: 一把巨大的巨剑靠在桌边。{w}\n完全无人看管，像是有人把它落在这儿了。{w}\n是故意放这儿的，还是弄丢了？

column5: Hey, this is almost a replica of mine.\nWhoever uses this has {i}fine{/i} taste.
column6: 嘿，这几乎和我那把一模一样。\n用这把剑的人{i}品味{/i}不错。

column5: It's been there ever since I got here.\nI have no idea who it belongs to...
column6: 我到这儿的时候它就在那儿了。\n我完全不知道它属于谁……

column5: Knowing Airen, it might be for decoration.\nIt's a shame though, it'll just rust away.\nA blade like this {i}needs{/i} to experience combat.
column6: 以我对艾琳的了解，说不定只是装饰用的。\n不过真可惜，它只会慢慢生锈。\n这样的剑{i}需要{/i}经历战斗。

column5: Oh, so you want to spar with me?\nI thought you'd never ask, Ulric.
column6: 哦，所以你是想跟我切磋？\n我还以为你永远不会开口呢，乌尔里克。

column5: That's not what I meant.
column6: 我不是那个意思。

column5: But before Ulric even finishes, Pro grabs the blade.\nStraining his entire body, he fails to lift it off the ground.
column6: 可乌尔里克话还没说完，普洛就抓住了那把剑。\n他全身用力，却没能把它从地上提起来。

column5: What!? Is it glued down...?
column6: 什么！？它是粘在地上了吗……？

column5: No, you're just weak.
column6: 不，只是你太弱了。

column5: Am not...!
column6: 才不是……！

column5: Wow, there's so much to choose from!
column6: 哇，可选的也太多了！

column5: Don't tell me you're planning on drinking, Fortaime.
column6: 别告诉我你打算喝酒，福泰姆。

column5: Why not...?
column6: 为什么不行……？

column5: We have a lot of stuff to do.
column6: 我们有很多事要做。

column5: But it looks so delicious...
column6: 可它看起来太好喝了……

column5: Trust me, it's probably not as tasty as you think.\nFrom what I've heard, it's just bitter, and it burns.
column6: 相信我，它大概没你想的那么好喝。\n据我所知，它又苦又辣嗓子。

column5: Sure, from what you've \"heard\".\nYou don't have to keep secrets from me, Valessa.
column6: 当然，“据你所知”。\n你不用对我保密，瓦莱莎。

column5: What are you talking about...!?\nI've never had any alcohol, I swear.
column6: 你在说什么啊……！？\n我从没喝过酒，我发誓。

column5: Don't worry, I {i}believe{/i} you.
column6: 别担心，我{i}相信{/i}你。

column5: Seriously...?
column6: 真的吗……？

column5: Aren't you two a little young to be drinking?
column6: 你们俩喝酒是不是太年轻了点？

column5: Nope! Valessa is just being a spoilsport.
column6: 才不呢！是瓦莱莎太扫兴了。

column5: I am {i}not{/i}!
column6: 我{i}才{/i}没有！

column5: Let's have some, then.
column6: 那我们就喝点吧。

column5: Well, maybe...
column6: 嗯，也许吧……

column5: Ah, yes. Peer pressure.
column6: 啊，对。从众压力。

column5: I walk up to the fireplace, watching it crackle and burn.{w}\nIt makes things really warm. Almost {i}too{/i} warm.{w}\nPeregrino would be fine without it.
column6: 我走到壁炉前，看着它噼啪燃烧。{w}\n它让这里真的很暖和。几乎{i}太{/i}暖和了。{w}\n佩雷格里诺没有它也完全没问题。

column5: Why is there a fireplace in here...?\nValinorth is always the perfect temperature.
column6: 这里为什么会有壁炉……？\n瓦利诺斯的温度一向恰到好处。

column5: Isn't that because of the spiritual energy?
column6: 那不是因为灵能量吗？

column5: Yeah, it keeps everything warm and cozy.\nWithout it, Valinorth would be an icy wasteland.
column6: 是啊，它让一切都温暖舒适。\n没有它，瓦利诺斯会是一片冰封的荒原。

column5: I think I saw the mountain peaks on my way up here.\nI wonder why the spirits chose {i}this{/i} place to settle down.
column6: 我上来的时候好像看到了那些山峰。\n我很好奇众灵为什么选了{i}这里{/i}定居。

column5: Oh, you must be talking about Eastcrown.\nEveryone wanders what's up there, but we'll never know.
column6: 哦，你说的肯定是东冠峰。\n人人都好奇那上面有什么，但我们永远不会知道。

column5: Don't say {i}never{/i}, Fortaime.\nI'm sure we'll figure it out one day.\nAlestia won't be unmapped forever.
column6: 别说{i}永远{/i}，福泰姆。\n我相信总有一天我们会弄清楚的。\n阿拉斯蒂亚不会永远是未知的。

column5: Not within our lifetimes, I'm sure.
column6: 我敢肯定，不会在我们有生之年。

column5: Probably not.
column6: 大概不会。

column5: Whoa, that got a little dark.
column6: 哇，这话有点沉重了。

column5: Good thing we have a fireplace to light things up.
column6: 还好我们有壁炉来点亮气氛。

column5: What are these shields here for...?
column6: 这些盾牌放在这儿是干什么的……？

column5: Mostly for design, I'm assuming.
column6: 我猜主要是装饰吧。

column5: Actually, I asked Airen about those.\nThey were used during the raid on The Triumvirate.\nYou know, the one where they stole the Blade of Exodus?
column6: 其实，我问过艾琳那些盾牌的事。\n它们是用在突袭三人执政团时留下的。\n你知道的，就是他们偷走流亡之刃那次？

column5: So it's in memoriam, then?
column6: 所以这是为了纪念咯？

column5: Something like that, yeah.\nAnd he said something about the fire in our hearts.\nThough I'm guessing that's related to the fireplace.
column6: 差不多吧，是啊。\n他还说了些关于我们心中火焰的话。\n不过我猜那跟壁炉有关。

column5: The man has a reason for everything, I guess.\nIt seems a lot of thought was put into this tavern.
column6: 看来这人做什么都有理由。\n这间酒馆似乎花了不少心思。

column5: Tavern...? Isn't it a bar?\nI've heard quite a few people call it Peregrino Bar.\nIn fact, they even started calling it PB for short.
column6: 酒馆……？这不是酒吧吗？\n我听到不少人叫它佩雷格里诺酒吧。\n事实上，他们甚至开始简称它为PB了。

column5: PB...? What an odd name.
column6: PB……？这名字真怪。

column5: Pro seems to be standing on the carpet, rubbing his feet on it.
column6: 普洛似乎正站在地毯上，用脚来回蹭着。

column5: Wow, this is so soft...!\nAiren must've cleaned it last night.
column6: 哇，这地毯好软……！\n艾琳昨晚肯定清理过。

column5: It is?
column6: 是吗？

column5: Hold on, let me see!
column6: 等等，让我看看！

column5: The three of them start doing it in unison.\nI exchange an awkward glance with Ulric as we watch.
column6: 他们三个开始齐刷刷地蹭了起来。\n我看着这一幕，和乌尔里克尴尬地对视了一眼。

column5: Seems like their priorities are in order.
column6: 看来他们分得清轻重缓急。

column5: Come on, you have {i}got{/i} to check this out!
column6: 来嘛，你{i}一定{/i}得来试试！

column5: I'll pass.
column6: 我就算了。

column5: Big barrels of ale decorate the back of the tavern.{w}\nThey must go through this stuff pretty fast.{w}\nIt'd warm up almost immediately.
column6: 酒馆后部摆着几大桶麦酒作装饰。{w}\n他们消耗这些东西肯定很快。{w}\n毕竟很快就会变温。

column5: A few patrons use the tap to fill up their cups.{w}\nAfter taking a sip, they throw coins into a nearby box.{w}\nAn honor system? That would be so easy to cheat.
column6: 几位顾客用龙头给自己倒满酒杯。{w}\n喝了一口后，他们把硬币丢进旁边的一个箱子里。{w}\n诚信自助？这也太容易作弊了。

column5: Wait — are these!?
column6: 等等——这些是！？

column5: Fortaime quickly runs to the table and grabs an apple.{w}\nAfter a large bite, and barely any chewing, he swallows.{w}\nA look of disappointment appears on his face shortly after.
column6: 福泰姆快步跑到桌前，抓起一个苹果。{w}\n他咬了一大口，几乎没怎么嚼就咽了下去。{w}\n很快，他脸上浮现出失望的表情。

column5: Of course they aren't...
column6: 当然不是……

column5: What's wrong with those...?\nLast time I checked, they were pretty tasty.
column6: 那些怎么了……？\n就我上次尝的，还挺好吃的。

column5: I was hoping it was a special kind of apple.\nMy parents used to bring me some from Mazeo all the time.\nBut the trading ban made it illegal to export them.
column6: 我还以为是什么特别的苹果。\n我父母以前总从马泽奥给我带一些回来。\n但贸易禁令让出口它们变成了非法。

column5: Oh, I think I know what you're talking about!\nThey sell them like crazy in the markets of Mazeo.
column6: 哦，我想我知道你说的是什么！\n在马泽奥的集市上，它们卖得可火了。

column5: Really!?\nYou {i}need{/i} to take me there, Pro!\nWe can make a brief detour, right?
column6: 真的吗！？\n你{i}一定{/i}得带我去那儿，普洛！\n我们可以稍微绕一下路，对吧？

column5: He looks at Ulric, with pleading eyes.
column6: 他用恳求的眼神看着乌尔里克。

column5: Maybe.
column6: 也许吧。

column5: Good enough for me!
column6: 对我来说够了！

column5: This party banter is affected by your choice to turn Peregrino into a barracks.
column6: 这段队伍闲聊会因你把佩雷格里诺改造成兵营的选择而有所不同。

column5: This party banter is affected by your choice to keep Peregrino as a tavern.
column6: 这段队伍闲聊会因你让佩雷格里诺保持酒馆原样的选择而有所不同。

column5: I make my way toward one of the private rooms. It's time to get some rest.{w}\nIt's been a long day,and the subsequent days show no signs of changing pace.{w}\nThis new life would simply be the nature of things. Everything was different.
column6: 我朝其中一间包房走去。该休息了。{w}\n今天真是漫长的一天，而接下来的日子也没有放缓的迹象。{w}\n这种新生活大概就是往后的常态了。一切都变了。

column5: I let that settle in for a while. It'd be almost impossible to sleep as things stood.{w}\nAll of our lives were flipped around in an instant. Not only that, but put in danger, too.{w}\nThere's no guarantee that any of us would survive this; and we didn't have a choice but to fight.
column6: 我让这个念头在心里沉淀了一会儿。就现状而言，几乎不可能睡得着。{w}\n我们所有人的生活都在一瞬间被彻底翻转。不仅如此，还被置于危险之中。{w}\n没人能保证我们谁都能活下来；而我们除了战斗别无选择。

column5: At least I didn't. Regardless of my feelings, I couldn't turn my back on Alestia.{w}\nIf I did that — I'd be saying my own life was more important than our entire world.{w}\nNo matter how hard I tried, there's no way I could convince myself that was true.
column6: 至少我没有选择。不管我心里怎么想，我都无法背弃阿拉斯蒂亚。{w}\n如果我那样做——就等于在说我的命比整个世界更重要。{w}\n无论怎么努力，我都没法说服自己那是真的。

column5: I sit on the edge of the bed, and let out a loud sigh as I lay back.
column6: 我坐在床边，躺下时长长地叹了口气。

column5: I don't get much rest before I'm shaken wide awake.{w}\nThe door to my room slowly opens. It's Valessa and Fortaime.{w}\nIt seems they've disregarded both my privacy {i}and{/i} desire to sleep.
column6: 我没休息多久就被人摇得彻底清醒。{w}\n房门缓缓打开。是瓦莱莎和福泰姆。{w}\n看来他们既无视了我的隐私，{i}也{/i}无视了我想睡觉的愿望。

column5: I rise up to greet them, unsure of what to say.
column6: 我起身迎接他们，不知道该说什么。

column5: Yeah, that's the long and short of it.\nFortaime and I have been talking for a while.\nThere's something we need to discuss. Now.
column6: 是啊，大致就是这样。\n我和福泰姆聊了一阵子了。\n有件事我们需要谈谈。就现在。

column5: Excuse me for trying to address something urgent!\nFortaime and I have been talking for a while.\nThere's something we need to discuss. Now.
column6: 抱歉，我只是想处理一件紧急的事！\n我和福泰姆聊了一阵子了。\n有件事我们需要谈谈。就现在。

column5: Good. Because we might be here for a while.\nFortaime and I have been talking all evening.\nThere's something we need to discuss. Now.
column6: 很好。因为我们可能要在这儿待一阵子了。\n我和福泰姆聊了一整晚。\n有件事我们需要谈谈。就现在。

column5: Hey, we need to talk. It's pretty important...\nFortaime and I have been talking all evening.
column6: 嘿，我们得谈谈。挺重要的……\n我和福泰姆聊了一整晚。

column5: Yeah, we both came to the same conclusion.\nThis isn't an order — it's more of a... \"polite demand\".
column6: 是啊，我们俩得出了同样的结论。\n这不是命令——更像是……“礼貌的要求”。

column5: [firstname]? You {i}need{/i} to choose the next Elder of Valinorth.
column6: [firstname]？你{i}必须{/i}选出瓦利诺斯的下一任长老。

column5: [firstname]? You {i}need{/i} to choose the next Elder of Valinorth.
column6: [firstname]？你{i}必须{/i}选出瓦利诺斯的下一任长老。

column5: You have a lot on your plate. You can't handle everything responsibly.\nValinorth's future requires nothing but the utmost care and attention.\nWe can't expect you to lead Valinorth {i}and{/i} train with that blade.
column6: 你身上担子太重了。你没法负责任地处理每一件事。\n瓦利诺斯的未来需要最周全的关心与照料。\n我们不能指望你既领导瓦利诺斯，{i}又{/i}用那把剑训练。

column5: It's exactly like she said. \nListen, I know this may seem sudden to you.\nBut we've been talking about it for a while now.
column6: 就是她说的那样。\n听着，我知道这对你来说可能很突然。\n但我们已经讨论这事有一阵子了。

column5: We wouldn't feel comfortable leaving Peregrino without a new Elder.\nSomeone needs to plot Valinorth's future, and make choices along the way.\nConsidering you'll be busy with The Rebellion, we want you to elect one of {i}us{/i}.
column6: 让佩雷格里诺没有新长老就离开，我们会不安心。\n总得有人规划瓦利诺斯的未来，沿途做出抉择。\n考虑到你会忙于反抗军的事务，我们希望你从{i}我们{/i}之中选一位。

column5: Valessa nods, and smiles. I can tell they're both dead serious.
column6: 瓦莱莎点头微笑。我看得出他们俩都是极其认真的。

column5: Let us carry this burden, [firstname]. Please.
column6: 让我们来扛这份重担吧，[firstname]。求你了。

column5: Let us carry this burden, [firstname]. Please.
column6: 让我们来扛这份重担吧，[firstname]。求你了。

column5: I rub the fatigue out of my eyes and stare at them for a few moments.{w}\nIt seemed that lately, people had a tendency of putting me on the spot.{w}\nTheir intentions were pure, however. To stop me from being overwhelmed.
column6: 我揉了揉疲惫的眼睛，盯着他们看了一会儿。{w}\n最近似乎人人都倾向于把我推到风口浪尖。{w}\n不过他们的用意是好的。是为了不让我被压垮。

column5: Any effort to alleviate the pressure shouldn't go unnoticed.{w}\nI cross my arms and continue to stare at them. They look concerned.{w}\nThis is almost like an \"intervention\". I doubt they'll leave without results.
column6: 任何缓解压力的努力都不该被忽视。{w}\n我抱起双臂，继续盯着他们。他们看起来有些担忧。{w}\n这几乎像是一场“劝诫会”。我怀疑他们不达目的是不会走的。

column5: Did we say something wrong?\nLook, he has no idea what to say.
column6: 我们是不是说错什么了？\n你看，他都不知道该说什么了。

column5: And I thought we made our case pretty clear.\nLook. We're the best two candidates, [firstname].\nYou should make your choice before the night is over.
column6: 我还以为我们已经把道理说得很清楚了。\n听着。我们就是最合适的两位人选，[firstname]。\n你该在今晚结束前做出选择。

column5: Did we say something wrong?\nLook, she has no idea what to say.
column6: 我们是不是说错什么了？\n你看，她都不知道该说什么了。

column5: And I thought we made our case pretty clear.\nLook. We're the best two candidates, [firstname].\nYou should make your choice before the night is over.
column6: 我还以为我们已经把道理说得很清楚了。\n听着。我们就是最合适的两位人选，[firstname]。\n你该在今晚结束前做出选择。

column5: We can talk about it a little more, if you'd like.\nIt'd be best if this wasn't a hasty choice, right?\nLet's think things through — like a team.
column6: 如果你愿意，我们可以再多谈一会儿。\n最好别仓促做决定，对吧？\n我们像一支队伍那样，把事情好好想清楚。

column5: There goes that rest we wanted to have.\nLooks like I'll have to get comfortable.
column6: 我们想休息的计划泡汤了。\n看来我得找个舒服的姿势待着了。

column5: She makes her way to the back of the room, and sits on the chest.{w}\nIt seems uncomfortable, even for a makeshift chair, but she doesn't show it.{w}\nFortaime yawns and rests his back against the windowsill, whistling innocently.
column6: 她走到房间后面，坐在箱子上。{w}\n就算当临时椅子，那看着也不舒服，但她没表现出来。{w}\n福泰姆打了个哈欠，背靠在窗台上，若无其事地吹着口哨。

column5: So, what do we talk about...?
column6: 那么，我们谈什么……？

column5: Like we said, ruling Valinorth requires a lot of attention.\nQuite frankly — we don't think you have enough to spare.\nNot with The Rebellion and that blade in the mix, at least.
column6: 就像我们说的，治理瓦利诺斯需要投入大量精力。\n坦白说——我们认为你没有那么多余力。\n至少，在反抗军和那把剑掺和进来的情况下。

column5: We just want to {i}help{/i} you.\nFor example, that choice about Peregrino?\nYou could've left it to us instead of stressing out about it.
column6: 我们只是想{i}帮{/i}你。\n比如，关于佩雷格里诺的那个选择？\n你本可以交给我们，而不是为此焦头烂额。

column5: Doesn't it make more sense to do that in the future?\nThat way, it won't interfere with your training.\nYou need to give that blade {i}all{/i} of your effort.
column6: 以后这样做不是更合理吗？\n那样就不会干扰你的训练。\n你得把你{i}全部{/i}的心力都投入到那把剑上。

column5: Yeah, and we really are the best two candidates.\nThere's no need to worry about making the wrong choice, here.\nI'm sure that both of us would lead Valinorth to a {i}great{/i} future.
column6: 是啊，而且我们俩确实是最合适的两位人选。\n不必担心在这里选错。\n我相信我们俩都能带领瓦利诺斯走向{i}辉煌{/i}的未来。

column5: But first things first — we need to reconnect with the spirits.\nThere's no point settling down on condemned land.\nWe'll have to ensure our future before we plan it out.
column6: 但首当其冲的是——我们需要重新与众灵建立联系。\n在被诅咒的土地上安顿下来毫无意义。\n我们得先确保未来，再去规划它。

column5: Yeah, he's right.\nAnything else...?
column6: 是啊，他说得对。\n还有别的吗……？

column5: Well, I'm actually a fan of what Mylus and his Father have done.\nValinorth has spent more than enough time being \"independent\".\nWe need to band together. We'll be strong enough to face any threat.
column6: 嗯，其实我很欣赏迈勒斯和他父亲所做的一切。\n瓦利诺斯“独立”的时间已经够久了。\n我们得团结起来。这样我们才能强大到足以面对任何威胁。

column5: Valessa wants to maintain our independence. We can't have that.\nHow long until we're attacked again? The Triumvirate isn't our last enemy.\nAnd when that time comes, I want to have allies. We need to be {i}strong{/i}.
column6: 瓦莱莎想维持我们的独立。我们不能那样。\n距离我们再次遭到攻击还有多久？三人执政团不是我们最后的敌人。\n等到那时候，我希望有盟友。我们得{i}强大{/i}起来。

column5: I actually support your decision to turn this place into a barracks.\nWe need to have protection in the future. It'd be stupid not to.\nDamek has the right idea. I'm starting to dig the guy.
column6: 其实我支持你把这里改造成兵营的决定。\n我们将来需要保护。不这么做才蠢。\n达梅克的想法是对的。我开始欣赏这家伙了。

column5: To that end, I would've converted Peregrino into a barracks.\nI know you didn't, and I'm going to honor your choice.\nI'll be proud to lead Valinorth just as you left it.
column6: 为此，我本来会把佩雷格里诺改造成兵营。\n我知道你没有，而我会尊重你的选择。\n能按你留下的原样领导瓦利诺斯，我会很自豪。

column5: Is that all...?
column6: 就这些……？

column5: Because Mylus and his Father have given up Valinorth's soul.\nWe need to stand apart. Our culture, our line of Seers — they're special.\nValinorth was, and always should be, independent. It's just fact.
column6: 因为迈勒斯和他父亲放弃了瓦利诺斯的灵魂。\n我们需要自立。我们的文化，我们先知的血脉——都很特别。\n瓦利诺斯曾经独立，也理应永远独立。这就是事实。

column5: Whatever comes our way, we can handle it on our own.\nThat's the way it's been for thousands and thousands of years.\nThis is only happening because we stoked The Triumvirate's ire.
column6: 无论遇到什么，我们都能独自应对。\n几千年来一直如此。\n如今的事之所以发生，只是因为我们激起了三人执政团的怒火。

column5: That won't happen again, and Fortaime can't see that.\nHe wants to unite with the rest of Alestia, and give up our identity.\nWhy waste all of our resources preparing for something that won't happen.
column6: 那样的事不会再发生，而福泰姆看不到这一点。\n他想和阿拉斯蒂亚其他地方联合，放弃我们的身份。\n为什么要浪费我们所有资源，去防备一件不会发生的事。

column5: And to that end, why did you want to convert this place into a barracks?\nI think it's kind of beautiful on its own. It adds to our sense of culture.\nTurning it into a military operation we'll never use? I don't get it...
column6: 说到这个，你为什么要把这里改造成兵营？\n我觉得它本身就很美。它增添了我们文化的气息。\n把它变成一场我们永远用不上的军事行动？我不理解……

column5: I think you understand where I'm coming from.\nOtherwise, you would've turned this place into a barracks.\nIt's important to our identity. We can't just throw it away.
column6: 我想你明白我的立场。\n否则，你早就把这里改造成兵营了。\n它关乎我们的身份认同。我们不能就这么抛弃它。

column5: Any other questions...?
column6: 还有别的问题吗……？

column5: They both audibly gulp, anticipating my decision.{w}\nThis was it, I'd decide the direction of Valinorth's future.{w}\nIt would either be Fortaime's unity, or Valessa's independence.
column6: 两人都能听见地咽了口口水，等待着我的决定。{w}\n就是现在了，我将决定瓦利诺斯未来的方向。{w}\n要么是福泰姆的联合，要么是瓦莱莎的独立。

column5: Well, what is it...?
column6: 那么，是什么……？

column5: Please think this through...
column6: 请仔细考虑清楚……

column5: I chose Fortaime. He was right, we needed unity and strength in the future.{w}\nTeaming up with the other nations wasn't sacrificing our identity at all.{w}\nValessa was wrong. It was simply turning a new page in our books.
column6: 我选了福泰姆。他是对的，我们将来需要团结和力量。{w}\n与其他国家联手根本不是牺牲我们的身份。{w}\n瓦莱莎错了。这不过是翻开我们新的一页。

column5: Time moves forward, and things change. Valinorth was isolated long enough.{w}\nPerhaps it's that isolation that led to our downfall. We lacked strength.{w}\nUnder Fortaime's lead, and with my blessing, we'd find that strength.
column6: 时间向前，事物在变。瓦利诺斯孤立得够久了。{w}\n也许正是那种孤立导致了我们的败落。我们缺乏力量。{w}\n在福泰姆的带领下，加上我的祝福，我们会找回那份力量。

column5: Wow... Really...?\nThis is like a dream come true.\nI can't believe this is actually happening...!
column6: 哇……真的吗……？\n这就像梦想成真一样。\n我简直不敢相信这真的发生了……！

column5: Yeah, that's a fact.\nFortaime in charge of our nation...?\nYou realize what that means, don't you?
column6: 是啊，这是事实。\n福泰姆掌管我们的国家……？\n你明白这意味着什么，对吧？

column5: Yeah, it means we're finally a team!\nI won't just be \"tagging along\" anymore.\nThe three of us {i}are{/i} Valinorth, now.
column6: 当然，这意味着我们终于成了一支队伍！\n我不再只是“跟着凑数”了。\n如今我们三个{i}就是{/i}瓦利诺斯。

column5: We can travel the world together, creating alliances!\nAfter we save Alestia, we can reconnect with the spirits, too!\nWe'll have a huge network of allies — ready to take on any challenge.
column6: 我们可以一起周游世界，缔结同盟！\n等我们拯救了阿拉斯蒂亚，还能重新与众灵建立联系！\n我们会有一个庞大的盟友网络——随时准备迎接任何挑战。

column5: I'm going to change history. This is insane.\nThank you so much! I don't know what else to say...!
column6: 我要改变历史了。这太疯狂了。\n太感谢你了！我都不知道该说什么了……！

column5: Well, I have a few things to say.\nBut I think I need to get some sleep.
column6: 嗯，我倒是有几句话想说。\n但我想我得去睡一觉了。

column5: She stands up and walks toward the door.{w}\nBut before she leaves, she turns back to face me.{w}\nIt appears that she's hesitant, unsure if she should speak.
column6: 她站起来，朝门口走去。{w}\n但离开前，她转过身面对我。{w}\n她似乎有些犹豫，不确定该不该开口。

column5: I'm upset, I can't deny that fact.\nBut this won't change the way I treat either of you.\nI'm still your Scribe, and I'm still Fortaime's friend.
column6: 我很难过，这一点我不否认。\n但这不会改变我对待你们两人的方式。\n我依然是你的书记官，也依然是福泰姆的朋友。

column5: I'll get over this. I've gotten over much worse.\nI can still help Valinorth in my own way, right?\nIn the end, maybe this is for the best.
column6: 我会挺过去的。我挺过过更糟的事。\n我还能用自己的方式帮助瓦利诺斯，对吧？\n到最后，也许这样才是最好的。

column5: She walks out, without displaying much emotion at all.{w}\nWas she hurt? I made the choice that I thought was most fitting.{w}\nI guess I'd never know. I'll take her word for it. Things will be fine.
column6: 她走了出去，几乎没流露出什么情绪。{w}\n她受伤了吗？我做了我认为最合适的选择。{w}\n我想我永远不会知道了。我就信她的话吧。一切都会好的。

column5: This decision could never please both people, and I had to do it.{w}\nWhatever ramifications came of this — would be impossible to avoid.{w}\nI turn back to Fortaime, who looks extremely excited, and deep in thought.
column6: 这个决定不可能让两个人都满意，而我必须做出选择。{w}\n无论由此带来什么后果——都无法避免。{w}\n我转回头看向福泰姆，他看起来异常兴奋，陷入沉思。

column5: When we get to Mazeo, I'll be Valinorth's envoy!\nMeeting Damek will be completely different. It'll be diplomatic in nature.\nWe can discuss how to better utilize the bond between our nations.
column6: 等我们到了马泽奥，我就是瓦利诺斯的使节了！\n和达梅克的会面会完全不同。那将是外交性质的。\n我们可以讨论如何更好地利用两国之间的纽带。

column5: It's a good sign that he's already thinking about such things.{w}\nThis wasn't a light decision, and he'd have a lot of responsibilities.{w} \nIt'd change the way he approached our entire journey from here on out.
column6: 他已经开始考虑这些事，这是个好迹象。{w}\n这可不是个轻松的决定，他会有很多责任。{w}\n从此以后，这都会改变他对我们整段旅程的态度。

column5: Oh, I guess I shouldn't be thinking out loud.\nWouldn't be a good idea to give away my strategies.
column6: 哦，我猜我不该把想法说出来。\n泄露自己的策略可不是好主意。

column5: He winks at me, and starts walking toward the door.{w}\nBut like Valessa did a moment earlier, he hesitates.{w}\nDid he have something important to say before he left?
column6: 他冲我眨了眨眼，朝门口走去。{w}\n但就像刚才瓦莱莎那样，他犹豫了。{w}\n他是在离开前有什么重要的话要说吗？

column5: Hey uh, I was actually wanting to ask...\nDo you think I could stay in your room tonight?\nAll this talk about attacks, and stuff — it has me scared.
column6: 嘿，呃，其实我一直想问你……\n你觉得我今晚能睡在你房间吗？\n一直在说袭击啊之类的事——把我吓着了。

column5: I mean, I'd feel a little safer with friends nearby.\nI can sleep on the floor if you don't want me to bother you.\nYou won't even know I'm here, I can promise you that.
column6: 我是说，有朋友在身边我会觉得安全一点。\n如果你不想我打扰你，我可以睡地上。\n我保证，你甚至不会察觉我在这儿。

column5: Thanks! I was really hoping you'd say that.\nI won't make a sound, I promise!
column6: 谢谢！我真希望你会答应。\n我保证，一点声音都不会出！

column5: He quickly grabs a sheet and curls up on the floor.{w}\nI decide to leave him be, and return to my bed.{w}\nI'm so tired, I practically collapse on it.
column6: 他迅速抓了条床单，蜷在地板上。{w}\n我决定不去管他，回到自己床上。{w}\n我太累了，几乎是瘫倒上去的。

column5: Whoa, are you serious? Thanks!\nI didn't want to ask in case you weren't comfortable.\nBut I can't turn down the comfort of a warm bed.
column6: 哇，你是认真的吗？谢谢！\n我之前不敢问，怕你会不自在。\n但我没法拒绝一张暖床的舒适。

column5: He waits for me to get in the bed before he hops in.{w}\nThere's more than enough space for both of us to be comfortable.{w}\nBefore closing his eyes though, he turns to me, and speaks softly.
column6: 他等我上了床才跳上来。{w}\n空间足够我们俩都睡得舒服。{w}\n不过闭上眼前，他转向我，轻声说道。

column5: Thanks, [firstname]...
column6: 谢谢你，[firstname]……

column5: Thanks, [firstname]...
column6: 谢谢你，[firstname]……

column5: Oh, I understand. I didn't mean to be too forward.\nI guess I'll be fine on my own. Maybe I'll find Ulric.\nEither way, don't mind me. Get some rest, alright?
column6: 哦，我明白。我不是想太冒昧。\n我想我一个人也没问题。也许我去找乌尔里克。\n总之，别管我。你好好休息，好吗？

column5: He promptly leaves the room, letting out a loud yawn.{w}\nWhat an interesting evening. Just one thing after another.{w}\nBut with everything out of the way, it was finally time to rest.
column6: 他立刻离开房间，打了个大大的哈欠。{w}\n真是个有趣的夜晚。一件事接着一件事。{w}\n但既然事情都处理完了，终于该休息了。

column5: I make my way back to the bed, and practically collapse on it.{w}\nHopefully I'd get enough sleep for our journey to The Outlook.{w}\nI find the most comfortable position I can, and surrender to heavy eyelids.
column6: 我回到床边，几乎是瘫倒上去。{w}\n但愿我能睡足，应付前往瞭望台的旅程。{w}\n我找了个最舒服的姿势，任由沉重的眼皮合上。

column5: I needed to side with Valessa, she was right.{w}\nWe only got involved in this because of our alliance with Mazeo.{w}\nIf we maintained our independence, Valinorth would be safe and sound.
column6: 我需要站在瓦莱莎这边，她是对的。{w}\n我们卷进这一切，只是因为和马泽奥的联盟。{w}\n如果我们保持独立，瓦利诺斯会安然无恙。

column5: Not only that, but our culture, and hierarchy were important too.{w}\nThere'd be no place for Seers and Scribes in the rest of Alestia.{w}\nAfter this was all said and done, Valinorth would remain strong and free.
column6: 不仅如此，我们的文化和等级制度也很重要。{w}\n在阿拉斯蒂亚其他地方，先知和书记官将无处容身。{w}\n等这一切尘埃落定，瓦利诺斯仍会强大而自由。

column5: Yes! I knew we were on the same page!\nI can't thank you enough for this. Really.\nI was so scared that we'd lose Valinorth.
column6: 太好了！我就知道我们想法一致！\n真不知该怎么谢你。真的。\n我之前好怕我们会失去瓦利诺斯。

column5: She practically runs toward me and hugs me.{w}\nFortaime rolls his eyes and looks elsewhere.{w}\nI'm unsure if it was because of my choice, or the hug.
column6: 她几乎是小跑着过来抱住我。{w}\n福泰姆翻了个白眼，看向别处。{w}\n我不确定是因为我的选择，还是因为这个拥抱。

column5: Hey, Fortaime even gets a promotion, too!\nAs your Scribe, he can fill the gap I'm leaving.\nOh man, my head is {i}so{/i} full of ideas right now.
column6: 嘿，福泰姆甚至还升职了！\n作为你的书记官，他能填补我留下的空缺。\n天哪，我现在满脑子{i}全是{/i}点子。

column5: I'll have to discuss things with Damek more in-depth.\nThis is so cool. When we meet him, it'll be a meeting of nations.\nSince I'm our envoy, I'll work on sounding as professional as I can.
column6: 我得和达梅克更深入地讨论一些事情。\n这太酷了。我们见到他时，那将是一场国与国的会晤。\n既然我是我们的使节，我会努力让自己听起来尽可能专业。

column5: Sir Damek, it's a pleasure to meet you.\nNo wait, that sounds stupid. Sir Damek...?
column6: 达梅克阁下，很荣幸见到您。\n不，等等，这听起来好蠢。达梅克阁下……？

column5: Hey Valessa, calm down for a second.\nThis means I get to replace you as the Scribe?\nYou'll have to give me some last minute training, you know.
column6: 嘿，瓦莱莎，先冷静一下。\n这就是说我要接替你当书记官了？\n你知道，你得给我来点临阵特训。

column5: Oh, right. I guess you {i}are{/i} a little rusty.\nNo worries, I'll take good care of you.\nThings will go swimmingly. Trust me.
column6: 哦，对了。我想你{i}确实{/i}有点生疏了。\n别担心，我会好好带你的。\n一切都会顺顺利利的。相信我。

column5: It's clear that she's jubilant.{w}\nI don't think I've seen her this excited in a while.{w}\nThis would change the entire way she approached our journey.
column6: 她显然喜气洋洋。{w}\n我想我有一阵子没见过她这么兴奋了。{w}\n这将会彻底改变她对这段旅程的态度。

column5: I'm kind of confused though, [firstname].\nYou decided to turn this place into a barracks?\nThat goes directly against our desire for unity...
column6: 不过我有点困惑，[firstname]。\n你决定把这里改造成兵营？\n这直接违背了我们对团结的期望……

column5: I'm sure I'll get over it, but I'm getting mixed signals.\nEither way, I'm proud to lead Valinorth just as you left it.\nI won't undo your decision. I respect it — I'll make it work.
column6: 我相信我会释怀的，但我收到的是矛盾的信号。\n不管怎样，能按你留下的原样领导瓦利诺斯，我很自豪。\n我不会推翻你的决定。我尊重它——我会把它落到实处。

column5: I'm kind of confused though, [firstname].\nYou decided to turn this place into a barracks?\nThat goes directly against our desire for unity...
column6: 不过我有点困惑，[firstname]。\n你决定把这里改造成兵营？\n这直接违背了我们对团结的期望……

column5: I'm sure I'll get over it, but I'm getting mixed signals.\nEither way, I'm proud to lead Valinorth just as you left it.\nI won't undo your decision. I respect it — I'll make it work.
column6: 我相信我会释怀的，但我收到的是矛盾的信号。\n不管怎样，能按你留下的原样领导瓦利诺斯，我很自豪。\n我不会推翻你的决定。我尊重它——我会把它落到实处。

column5: And I just want to thank you even more, [firstname].\nYou decided to keep Peregrino the way it is. I'm grateful.\nThat's a {i}huge{/i} step toward our continued independence.
column6: 而且我更想谢谢你，[firstname]。\n你决定让佩雷格里诺保持原样。我很感激。\n那是朝着我们延续独立迈出的{i}巨大{/i}一步。

column5: And I just want to thank you even more, [firstname].\nYou decided to keep Peregrino the way it is. I'm grateful.\nThat's a {i}huge{/i} step toward our continued independence.
column6: 而且我更想谢谢你，[firstname]。\n你决定让佩雷格里诺保持原样。我很感激。\n那是朝着我们延续独立迈出的{i}巨大{/i}一步。

column5: Well, it seems like we have our work cut out for us.\nI'm a little upset that you didn't pick me, but I'll get over it.\nAt the end of the day, I'm not just \"tagging along\" anymore.
column6: 嗯，看来我们有的是活要干。\n你没选我，我有点难过，但我会释怀的。\n说到底，我不再只是“跟着凑数”了。

column5: The position of Elder has only been open for a day.\nBut I've been training to become a Scribe for my {i}entire life{/i}.\nMaybe, in this case, things worked out for the best.
column6: 长老之位空出来才一天。\n但我为了成为书记官已经训练了{i}一辈子{/i}。\n也许这件事，结果反而是最好的。

column5: He gives me a wide smile before walking toward the door.\nBut before he leaves, he turns back and looks at the both of us.
column6: 他冲我露出一个大大的笑容，然后朝门口走去。\n但离开前，他转过身，看着我们俩。

column5: You coming, Valessa?
column6: 你来吗，瓦莱莎？

column5: Oh, sure. Just give me a few more minutes.\nI have a few more things to talk about.
column6: 哦，好。再给我几分钟。\n我还有几件事要谈。

column5: Fair enough. G'night!
column6: 行吧。晚安！

column5: After he leaves, Valessa lets out a loud sigh.{w}\nShe presses her back against the wall, and closes her eyes.
column6: 他走后，瓦莱莎长长地叹了口气。{w}\n她把背靠在墙上，闭上了眼睛。

column5: For once, the future doesn't seem so uncertain.\nI'm sure I'll be put in a lot of complicated situations, [firstname].\nYour wisdom is just as important to Valinorth's future as I am.
column6: 这一次，未来似乎没那么不确定了。\n我肯定会被卷入许多复杂的处境，[firstname]。\n你的智慧对瓦利诺斯的未来，和我一样重要。

column5: For once, the future doesn't seem so uncertain.\nI'm sure I'll be put in a lot of complicated situations, [firstname].\nYour wisdom is just as important to Valinorth's future as I am.
column6: 这一次，未来似乎没那么不确定了。\n我肯定会被卷入许多复杂的处境，[firstname]。\n你的智慧对瓦利诺斯的未来，和我一样重要。

column5: Remember how you went to Mylus today? Instead of telling me?\nIf your visions involve my leadership, or Valinorth's safety, {i}please{/i} come to me.\nOtherwise, I'll train Fortaime to take good care of you. He's in good hands.
column6: 还记得你今天去找迈勒斯，却没告诉我吗？\n如果你的幻象涉及我的领导，或者瓦利诺斯的安全，{i}请{/i}来找我。\n否则，我会把福泰姆训练好，让他好好照顾你。你会被照顾得妥妥当当。

column5: She exits the room with what I can only describe as the utmost confidence.{w}\nHer posture, her steps, it all displayed something like a newborn resolve.{w}\nAnd for good reason, too — we just decided the direction of our nation's future.
column6: 她走出房间，那神态我只能形容为极度的自信。{w}\n她的姿态，她的步伐，都透出一种新生的决心。{w}\n这也难怪——我们刚刚决定了国家未来的方向。

column5: I make my way back to the bed, and practically collapse on it.{w}\nHopefully I'd get enough sleep for our journey to The Outlook.{w}\nSurrendering to heavy eyelids, I lose myself to the night.
column6: 我回到床边，几乎是瘫倒上去。{w}\n但愿我能睡足，应付前往瞭望台的旅程。{w}\n我任由沉重的眼皮合上，沉入夜色之中。

column5: It isn't much longer before we fall asleep.{w}\nBut much to my dismay — I'd get no rest that night.{w}\nFor the fates had something else in store.
column6: 没过多久我们就睡着了。{w}\n但让我沮丧的是——那晚我没能休息。{w}\n因为命运另有安排。

column5: It isn't much longer before I fall asleep.{w}\nBut much to my dismay — I'd get no rest that night.{w}\nFor the fates had something else in store.
column6: 没过多久我就睡着了。{w}\n但让我沮丧的是——那晚我没能休息。{w}\n因为命运另有安排。

column5: Before I can even comprehend what happened, I'm whisked away from Peregrino.{w}\nThis isn't a vision. Those don't happen so fast after falling asleep. This is different.{w}\nI rub my eyes, and try to take in more of my surroundings. Where am I...?
column6: 我还没来得及弄明白发生了什么，就被从佩雷格里诺卷走了。{w}\n这不是幻象。幻象不会在入睡后这么快出现。这不一样。{w}\n我揉揉眼睛，努力看清周围。我这是在哪儿……？

column5: It's so dark, with architecture unlike anything I've ever seen.{w} \nThere's nobody here, I'm all by myself. Except for {i}that{/i}.{w}\nAt the other end of the room, it pulsates, and glows.
column6: 这里一片漆黑，建筑风格是我从未见过的。{w}\n这里空无一人，只有我自己。除了{i}那个{/i}。{w}\n在房间的另一端，它脉动着，发着光。

column5: As I look at it, I feel something burn deep inside of me.{w}\nNot in a bad way, no, this is more like a burning desire.{w}\nIt's calling out to me. It wants me to get closer.
column6: 当我看着它时，我感到体内深处有什么在灼烧。{w}\n不是什么坏感觉，不，更像是强烈的渴望。{w}\n它在呼唤我。它想让我靠近。

column5: I take another step, and the pain returns to my body. But this time, it's worse!{w}\nI'm brought to my knees, and I can't seem to get back up. It's tearing me apart!{w}\nI pant heavily, unable to move as it continues to harm my spirit.
column6: 我又迈出一步，疼痛重新袭上身体。但这次更厉害！{w}\n我被压得跪倒在地，似乎再也起不来。它要把我撕裂了！{w}\n我剧烈地喘着气，动弹不得，而它仍在伤害我的灵。

column5: Stop.
column6: 停下。

column5: I immediately fall to the ground as I hear the voice from behind me.{w}\nBut it's not a bad thing, as I gain full control over my body.{w}\nWhatever was controlling me, they had put a stop to it.
column6: 身后传来声音，我立刻跌倒在地。{w}\n但这不是坏事，因为我重新完全掌控了自己的身体。{w}\n不管之前是什么在操控我，他们让它停下了。

column5: I turn around, and take steps toward them, grateful.{w}\nI could tell the farther away from that object I was, the better.{w}\nBut when I reach this mysterious person, I'm not prepared for what I see.
column6: 我转过身，心怀感激地朝他们走去。{w}\n我能感觉到，离那个东西越远越好。{w}\n但当我走到这个神秘人面前时，眼前的景象让我毫无准备。

column5: It's almost instinctual now. Interesting.\nSorry for not being here right away. I didn't know you'd come so fast.\nThat means things have slowed down on your end. I see...
column6: 现在几乎成了本能。有意思。\n抱歉没能立刻出现。我没想到你来得这么快。\n那说明你那边的进展慢下来了。我明白了……

column5: The Triumvirate. I can tell right away.{w}\nOr at least, one of them, since I only see one cloak before me.{w}\nI start to panic, and reach for the Blade of Exodus.
column6: 三人执政团。我一眼就认出来了。{w}\n或者至少是其中一位，因为我面前只有一件斗篷。{w}\n我惊慌起来，伸手去摸流亡之刃。

column5: No.
column6: 不。

column5: They wave their hand forward, and I can no longer move.{w}\nLetting out a chuckle, they start walking toward me.
column6: 他们向前一挥手，我就再也动不了了。{w}\n他们轻笑一声，朝我走来。

column5: Even now, corruption grows within you.\nIt can flow from the most {i}noble{/i} of actions.\nBut is that corruption what you truly want...?
column6: 即便现在，腐化仍在你体内滋长。\n它可能源于最{i}高尚{/i}的行为。\n但那份腐化真是你想要的吗……？

column5: So you remain pure, even now. Interesting.\nI expected to see the seeds of corruption within you.\nIs it possible you know...? No, that can't be right.
column6: 所以你至今仍然纯净。有意思。\n我本以为会在你体内看到腐化的种子。\n难道你已经知道了……？不，那不可能。

column5: There is no way to discern the consequences of your actions.\nYou act instinctively, much like before. You do what you think is right.\nBut what is right, and what is pure — well, those are two different things.
column6: 你无法看透自己行为的后果。\n你和从前一样凭本能行事。你只做你认为对的事。\n但何为正确，何为纯净——那可是两回事。

column5: They strike a pose, as if they're lost in thought.
column6: 他们摆出个姿势，仿佛陷入了沉思。

column5: You know who I am. Or at least, what I belong to.\nI speak not for The Triumvirate, but of my own accord.\nNot that this would go against the wishes of my subordinates.
column6: 你知道我是谁。或者至少，知道我属于什么。\n我不是代表三人执政团说话，而是出于我自己的意愿。\n倒不是说这会违背我下属们的意愿。

column5: Subordinates...?{w}\nDoes this mean I'm in the presence of The Triumvirate's leader?
column6: 下属……？{w}\n难道说我正面对着三人执政团的首领？

column5: That power within you is a truly wonderful thing.\nSo much strength, gifted to you by the realm of spirits.\nBut you have to ask yourself — is it truly a gift...?
column6: 你体内的那份力量真是奇妙。\n如此强大的力量，是灵界赐予你的。\n但你得问问自己——它真的是一份馈赠吗……？

column5: Do you act in Alestia's best interests? Or in the spirits?\nUntil now, everyone in Valinorth assumed that the two aligned.\nBut things are changing. They're starting to make a push.
column6: 你是为阿拉斯蒂亚的最大利益行事？还是为众灵？\n直到如今，瓦利诺斯所有人都以为二者是一致的。\n但情况在变。他们开始有所行动了。

column5: I strain myself, trying to move, but to no avail.{w}\nWhatever they've done, they've taken over control of my body.
column6: 我拼命挣扎想动，却毫无用处。{w}\n不管他们做了什么，他们已经接管了我身体的控制权。

column5: What purpose is your journey if it ends in complete corruption...?\nKeep that in mind as you stride forward, and make those tough choices.\nMany of them breed corruption. The pursuit of strength, for example.
column6: 如果你的旅程以彻底的腐化告终，那又有什么意义……？\n在你大步前行、做出那些艰难抉择时，请记住这一点。\n其中许多会滋生腐化。比如对力量的追求。

column5: Before you go, I did call you here for one purpose.
column6: 在你离开之前，我叫你来这里确实有一个目的。

column5: They motion to the idol at the back of the room, before waving their arm.{w}\nAs the ability to move returns to my body, I stumble, failing to balance myself.{w}\nHow is it possible to do this...? Can they manipulate spiritual energy without the blade?
column6: 他们指向房间后方的灵像，然后一挥手。{w}\n当身体恢复行动能力时，我踉跄了一下，没能站稳。{w}\n这怎么可能做到……？他们不用那把剑就能操控灵能量吗？

column5: I regain my balance, and immediately turn to look at the idol.
column6: 我稳住身形，立刻转头看向那尊灵像。

column5: It's beautiful, isn't it...?\nThere's never been a more {i}pure{/i} form of corruption.\nYou seek to dethrone us — isn't that your goal?
column6: 它很美，不是吗……？\n从未有过比这更{i}纯粹{/i}的腐化形态。\n你想推翻我们——那不是你的目标吗？

column5: In that case, remember one thing.
column6: 既然如此，记住一件事。

column5: They tilt their head, and though I can't see their face, I assume they're smiling.{w}\nWith a final wave of their hand, I collapse to the ground, and my vision fades away.
column6: 他们歪了歪头，虽然我看不见他们的脸，但我猜他们在微笑。{w}\n他们最后挥了一下手，我倒在地上，视野渐渐消散。

column5: The only thing that can destroy pure corruption — is purity itself, embodied.
column6: 唯一能摧毁纯粹腐化之物——是纯净本身的化身。

column5: I hear their words, but I seem to exist in a void of nothingness.{w}\nI don't understand what just happened. I'm only left with a multitude of questions.{w}\nMy actions can influence the purity or corruption of the power inside of me...?
column6: 我听见他们的话，却仿佛置身于一片虚无之中。{w}\n我不明白刚才发生了什么。只剩下满腹疑问。{w}\n我的行为竟能影响体内力量的纯净或腐化……？

column5: That doesn't make any sense. But then again, maybe that's what they wanted.{w}\nThey'd want to confuse me — to try and push me down a different path.{w}\nOf course they'd want to scare me away from decisions that would harm their reign.
column6: 这根本说不通。但话说回来，也许这正是他们想要的。{w}\n他们就是想迷惑我——试图把我推上另一条路。{w}\n他们当然想把我吓退，不去做那些会危害他们统治的决定。

column5: Or would they...?
column6: 又或者，他们真会这样吗……？

column5: I take one step forward, keeping my eyes on the mysterious object.{w}\nAs soon as my foot lands on the ground, pain courses through my body.{w}\nI'm brought to my knees. It's almost like it's slowly draining my energy!
column6: 我向前迈出一步，目光紧盯着那个神秘的东西。{w}\n我的脚刚一落地，疼痛便贯穿全身。{w}\n我被压得跪倒在地。它简直像在慢慢抽干我的能量！

column5: When it subsides, I stand back up. But the desire hasn't gone away.{w}\nI need to get closer. I need to know {i}exactly{/i} what this thing is.{w}\nMy burning curiosity trumps any care for my own well-being.
column6: 疼痛消退后，我重新站起来。但那份渴望并未消失。{w}\n我需要靠近些。我需要{i}确切地{/i}知道这东西是什么。{w}\n我强烈的求知欲压过了对自身安危的在意。

column5: Even though I object to such a mindset, I keep moving forward.{w}\nIt's almost like my body is moving on its own, without my input.
column6: 尽管我反对这种心态，我还是继续向前。{w}\n简直就像我的身体在自己移动，不必我发号施令。

column5: Almost immediately, I find myself back in Peregrino. I got no sleep.{w}\nAnd thanks to what just happened, I doubt I would on any other night.{w}\nThe lingering fright that this made happen again — was almost crippling.
column6: 几乎转眼间，我又回到了佩雷格里诺。我一夜没睡。{w}\n拜刚才那事所赐，我想别的夜晚我也睡不着了。{w}\n那种挥之不去的恐惧，生怕它再次发生——几乎让人瘫软。

column5: The sun shines through the window, illuminating the room.{w}\nI can see how covered in dust everything is. Overnight patrons must be rare.{w}\nAs I scan the room, I notice an entire section is dust free. Fortaime is cleaning.
column6: 阳光透过窗户照进来，照亮了房间。{w}\n我能看到到处都蒙着厚厚的灰尘。留宿的客人肯定很少。{w}\n我环视房间，注意到有一整块地方没有灰尘。福泰姆在打扫。

column5: Oh, hey! Good morning, [firstname].\nI saw all this dust, and couldn't help myself.\nSure, it lost me a few hours of sleep, but I don't care.
column6: 哦，嘿！早上好，[firstname]。\n看到这么多灰尘，我实在忍不住。\n是，这让我少睡了几小时，但我不在乎。

column5: Oh, hey! Good morning, [firstname].\nI saw all this dust, and couldn't help myself.\nSure, it lost me a few hours of sleep, but I don't care.
column6: 哦，嘿！早上好，[firstname]。\n看到这么多灰尘，我实在忍不住。\n是，这让我少睡了几小时，但我不在乎。

column5: How about you? How did you sleep?
column6: 你呢？睡得怎么样？

column5: Awesome, we need all the energy we can get!\nBy the way, I think I heard them talking outside.\nSomething about skipping breakfast, and eating in Mazeo.
column6: 太好了，我们正需要尽可能多的精力！\n对了，我好像听到他们在外面聊天。\n说什么不吃早饭，到马泽奥再吃。
